newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania liberalises exports of grain.
newsitem.headline: Romania liberalises exports of grain.

text.p: Romania has liberalised grain exports following moves by the government to cut subsidies to the farming sector, the state news agency Rompres said on Monday.
Quoting Industry Ministry sources, Rompres said exports of wheat flour, bread, maize, barley and sunflower meal had been liberalised starting Monday.
Trading companies previously had to apply for export licences to export these commodities, until recently subsidised by the state.
The new centrist government headed by Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea has pledged to restructure the farming sector, including cuts in subsidies.

Rompres said exports of milling wheat would be fully liberalised starting August 15, when Romania is expected to harvest its 1997 wheat crop. Until then, companies willing to export wheat would have to apply for export licences, it said.
